<reason>Side B won decisively by trapping Side A in two fatal contradictions while defending a well-grounded case on civic reciprocity and fan atmosphere. First, Side A opened by arguing that dynamic pricing helps budget-conscious locals find cheap seats, but later described dynamic general sales as a "bloodbath of bots and speed" and explicitly conceded in Rebuttal 2 that dynamic markets "fail locals during sell-out surges." Side B rightly weaponized this concession to show why an unreserved dynamic market prices out the host community when events actually matter. Second, Side B dismantled Side A's "means-tested discounts" counter-proposal, showing that verifying tax or welfare records is far more invasive than checking a billing postal code or membership history, and that Side A applied a blatant double standard by claiming account-linked local reserves would be scalped while account-linked low-income discounts magically could not be resold. Side B also cleanly answered the traveling-fan objection via the motion's "or members" clause and solved the emergency-refund issue via face-value return exchanges—a point Side A simply ignored in its closing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's pressure questions [B3.1-B3.2] and follow-through in [B4.3-B4.4] and [B5.1-B5.2], which forced Side A to concede that dynamic markets fail locals during high-demand surges [A4.1] and exposed Side A's double standard on means-tested discounts versus local reserves.</best_rebuttal>
